reviews.text: I’m furious with Webster Veterinarian Center after what they put my dog Luke through on September 30th 2026.  I brought him in for red marks on his head and they charged me 121 dollars for the emergency visit and around 560 dollars for blood work, then sent us home like nothing was wrong.  Hours later Luke got drastically worse, so I rushed him to AMC Hospital downtown.  The ER vet there took one look and said it was life or death and admitted him immediately.  The difference was shocking.  One vet missed how serious this was and the other saw it instantly without even waiting on blood work.  As of October 2nd 2026 they still haven’t called me with dog's results.  If I’d trusted Webster, my dog would be dead right now.  That’s negligence, plain and simple.  Do not take your pet here.  Go to AMC instead if you care about your animal.. And the best advice I can give you is to get pet insurance because it will alleviate the expenses. I am here to support all pet moms and dads.

We have visited this clinic previously and have consistently received exceptional service. Today, I brought our family dog, Blackie, who is 12 years old, for an appointment. The visit was for an EKG because of a heart murmur. Mark, the receptionist, was polite and courteous. Dr. Gilbert examined Blackie with assistants Stella and Alisha. I appreciated the clarity they provided my mother and me about the necessary exams and services. They explained everything plainly, which kept us comfortable and confident. They even offered a payment plan called “cherry” to help manage the substantial cost for Blackie’s care. Unfortunately, we had to leave Blackie for a couple of hours so the tests could be completed. They called us with a courtesy update about the pickup time. When I returned, I waited 15 minutes; during that time, I used the restroom, where the cleaner, Christian, was respectful and courteous. He told me he would finish soon, and I replied, “no rush.” He completed the work, leaving the restroom cleaned, disinfected, stocked with toilet paper and soap. It smelled great, and he did an excellent job. I learned his name and want to give a huge shout-out to that young man. Once Blackie was ready, Dr. Gilbert, Stella, and Alisha thoroughly explained the medication and a follow-up appointment in two weeks.

My overall experience was fantastic—I must say it was better than the ASPCA on 161st in the Bronx.

I wanted to provide a better review for this veterinary center given its location, mission to the surrounding community, cost, and welcoming environment. However, there were several factors that lead me to urge others to carefully consider these issues before bringing their senior pet here.

1. When we arrived, we waited approximately 30 minutes to be seen by the veterinary technician. They did not have the medical records that I had previously emailed because one of their technicians had provided me with the incorrect email address (I copied and pasted the email address they sent me specifically to avoid this issue in the first place.) Nevertheless, I re-sent the records and tried to provide the most pertinent medical history to facilitate the visit.

2. The veterinary technician used the incorrect needle gauge while administering vaccinations. This was noted by the veterinarian after the vaccination had been administered, and she did address it with the technician. I understand that mistakes happen, but I did see my dog become visibly uncomfortable during the process.

3. I had to reach out to the office multiple times by phone and text after missing one call from the veterinarian regarding my dog's senior lab work. I assumed there was nothing particularly concerning given that the office continued to delay the call back and stated that a nurse would call me with the results. When I was finally able to speak with the veterinarian, she was thorough and informed me about some liver issues my dog may be experiencing. This definitely came as a surprise, particularly because he needs to take supplements for at least the next month. Given this information, I was surprised by the lack of urgency in communicating the results.

4. I also had to reach out multiple times to discuss my pet's heart medications. I was told that the medication had been sent to a pharmacy that (a) I had not confirmed was the best option and (b) I had never heard of and have been unable to reach.

5. This is a minor issue, but the center uses voice recordings and AI to facilitate notetaking and visit summaries. While I understand that this can improve efficiency, and there are signs in the office indicating that recording is taking place, I believe full transparency and informed consent should be addressed at the beginning of the appointment.

Overall, the experience has been extremely time-consuming. I understand that things happen and that no veterinary practice is perfect. However, the major systems at this location including those responsible for medical records, medication management, and patient inquiries need to be reviewed and optimized. These issues have made what should have been a straightforward visit and follow-up process unnecessarily difficult, particularly when caring for a senior pet who relies on timely and consistent medical care.

The options they highlighted off the list handed to me were also unable to operate and redirected me to AMC. of course when I try calling back at 5:26 there is no urgency to pick up.

Will likely not return, while they have a slightly higher base examination fee I would recommend Animal Medical Center as first choice. Today I brought my kittens, Oreo and Luna, in for their annual checkup and vaccinations. Jazz and Bre were very kind and sweet with my kittens, and the doctor was very kind as well.

First time visiting
1st thing- Signs do not really direct you to the front door, not a huge issue, someone was walking in so that confusion was quickly resolved

When you walk in, the staff is very welcoming. Once you check in you are required to pay up front (this is new to me) to which I did. I was taken to a room where the preliminary examination was done by one of the techs (again very nice staff), they take my pet to the back to preform a test, once he was brought back I was told to wait for vaccines, they asked I wait in the general waiting room, this was about 3:30ish, my foolish self just patiently waited and about 5pm feeling that it may have been too long to wait I asked about the vaccines.

This is where they went downhill fast, THEY FORGOT about my pet and just left me waiting, there is an enormous staff and not one of them realized.

What this showed to me was that either they are very unorganized (with so many people, HOW??) and that for them it is only a job and not something that they are passionate about, if I were the manager I would be embarrassed of the poor organization skills.

Once we were brought back again to exam room, the Dr came in somewhat quickly but it was too late, I felt my time was wasted.

Another thing is that I thought this was a low cost veterinarian but nope, this is an independent provider, remember me saying they made me pay up front, well guess what, I was told I overpaid and I would have a credit (it was not much but still an overcharge).

I asked for an estimate on neutering and it was a lil above $600 (this includes the neuter and other items such as a chip and an additional service). This was an insane price as I went to this location believing it to be low cost, for the money they charge for the visits A LOT more is expected, especially my time not being wasted. I do want to point out that it was not even busy! (this was stated by one of the workers to another pet parent.

What would I change:
1- more organization, there is no reason to be left off the board, the movement to next step should be seamless-

2. Don't pre charge if the pricing is not accurate

3. Re-evaluate whether all the employees are truly needed seeing how the ball is being dropped consistently.

4. Send after visit surveys to truly see how people perceive the service.

I will unfortunately need to go in one more time for a second vaccine but I will definitely be looking for a more organized facility where I feel like my time is being respected and my pet is treated like he matters- and the reason I say this is that no pet especially a cat likes to be in a place where there are other animals for more time than they should be.

I chose this clinic for Smoky’s neuter surgery because their prices were lower than most places. To start with the positives: the staff is very friendly, the procedure prices are affordable, and Smoky’s neuter surgery itself went very well.

Unfortunately, everything that happened after that was extremely stressful.

The day after the surgery, Smoky started vomiting nonstop and couldn’t keep any food or water down. I rushed him to the ER overnight where he received an anti-nausea injection. About 24 hours later, once the injection wore off, the vomiting started again. I brought him back to this clinic where they checked his vitals, did X-rays (which were normal), and said they administered another anti-nausea injection.

During that visit, an assistant took Smoky to another room for the injection and X-rays. When he was brought back, the assistant told me the injection had already been given. However, when the doctor came in a few minutes later, she seemed unaware that the injection had supposedly been administered. I confirmed with the assistant that it had been done and left trusting that everything was handled.

Less than 24 hours later, Smoky was vomiting again (injection is supposed to last 24 hrs).

That same day, my two other cats at home developed the exact same symptoms. This strongly suggested a stomach virus or food poisoning rather than something surgery-related. I took those two cats to our regular veterinarian. There, everything was done in front of me: vitals were taken, blood and stool tests were run, they received an anti-nausea injection and fluids, and — most importantly — they were sent home with four days of anti-nausea medication. That single visit resolved their symptoms.

Smoky, however, had never been prescribed anti-nausea medication for home use. Because his stomach remained sensitive, he kept vomiting and couldn’t keep food down. I had to bring him back to this clinic again. By this point I had an important piece of information: my other two cats had the same illness.

Despite that, the clinic insisted Smoky needed another X-ray to rule out an obstruction. They saw nothing but recommended sending the X-rays to a specialist for confirmation (which cost around $700). The specialist also found nothing.

This is where things became very concerning. With multiple cats showing the same symptoms, two clear X-rays, and a radiology specialist confirming no obstruction, one of the doctors suggested EXPLORATORY SURGERY AS A PLAN A — a major surgery costing around $5,000. Plan B was to hospitalize him for 24 hours and observe.

I chose to hospitalize him and when I picked Smoky up the next day, he was stable but they still weren’t planning to send him home with anti-nausea medication. Based on my experience with my other cats, I specifically requested the prescription, and only then was it provided.

After that, Smoky recovered. Weeks later, all of my cats are doing fine.

However, the stress my cat and I went through was completely unnecessary. In the end, this experience cost far more than treating my other two cats at a “less affordable” veterinarian. For comparison, I ended up paying $2,500 for Smoky’s treatment (no including the neutering surgery or the ER visit which was done at another center) and for my other 2 cats combined I paid $850.

More importantly, Smoky was put at risk of an invasive surgery that — based on everything we now know — was never needed.

I have since requested Smoky’s medical records and will not be bringing him back here.

Bottom line I do not recommend for any exotic pet. I don't think Dr. Ritchie has enough experience and I would not trust her judgment. If you can't diagnosis without imaging for parasites or respiratory issues or infection what is the point of coming here? Another thing they do not have any imaging for exotics so basically come here and spend $125 to have her listen to the basic vitals.
